lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Riverside Cinema | Box Office Attendant | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Sold tickets and concessions during evening shifts and balanced the cash drawer at close.
- Trained 3 new attendants on the ticketing system and the refund policy.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality.
items.because: These personal details do not help readers assess the candidate’s qualifications and are conventionally left off.

items.says: Education appears before Experience despite several years of relevant work.
items.because: The current order leads with the degree rather than the candidate’s analytical experience.

items.says: The duties do not state what they achieved.
items.because: Without an outcome, the bullet reads like a list of routine duties.

items.says: Past-tense verbs make recurring work in a current role sound ended.
The training bullet does not state what the training achieved.
items.because: The count and topics do not show whether attendants could work independently or handle tickets and refunds accurately.

items.says: The training bullet should come before the less distinctive duties bullet.
The cinema role is disconnected from the analytics direction and takes up too much space.
items.because: Two bullets give a less relevant position more prominence than the current analytics work.

items.says: The dashboard bullet does not show how retention patterns were identified or presented.
The join method is reversed, and counting null customer names does not reliably find customers with no orders.
items.because: A left join from orders cannot reveal customers with no orders, and customers with orders can have null names.

items.says: The line does not say what finding customers with no orders changed or enabled.
items.because: Without a consequence, the analysis has no visible value.

items.says: The detailed join-and-count explanation distracts from the finding.
items.because: The mechanics take up space and make the result harder to scan.

items.says: The long list of methods buries the increase in orders tied to a campaign.
items.because: Readers reach several technical tasks before the 58%-to-81% result.

items.says: The funding outcome appears after the presentation detail.
items.because: That makes the result harder to catch.

items.says: Stopping at the first daily p-value below 0.05 does not support calling the test significant.
items.because: Repeated checks under an unadjusted threshold raise the false-positive rate above 5%.

items.says: The test bullet does not say what the test found or changed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether checkout performance improved or what decision the test supported.

items.says: The lengthy account of p-value checks leaves the test’s result unstated.
items.because: Process detail crowds out information that would show the test’s value.

items.says: The analysis description does not show how it identified the evening peak.
The call-center outcome should lead the entry.
“My findings” uses a first-person pronoun.
“Writes” is present tense even though the role ended in July 2022.
items.because: The verb makes the timing inconsistent and may imply the guide is still being written.

items.says: Unrelated duties bury the time saving and obscure which work produced it.
items.because: The saving follows several tasks, so its cause is unclear.

items.says: The line does not identify the tool or approach used to automate the extract.
The Pinecrest role does not clearly focus on its analytical work.
items.because: Bullets spanning testing, operations, documentation and support make the core contribution harder to recognize.

items.says: The percentage MAE has no stated basis.
items.because: Readers cannot interpret the error without its denominator or normalization.

items.says: The modeling approach is not identified.
items.because: Python and SQL do not show the approach behind the forecast.

items.says: The change from 300 to 200 hours is a 33.3% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: The decrease is 100 hours from a baseline of 300.

items.says: The replay description does not say what rebalancing change was tested.
items.because: The replay setting alone does not explain what was changed.

items.says: The empty-station-hours result should lead the project bullets.
The wording can make the replay result sound like an observed operational result.
items.because: It says hours were cut before revealing that the reduction was in a replay.

items.says: The change from 60% to 75% is 15 percentage points, not a 15% increase.
items.because: Relative to the starting rate of 60%, the increase is 25%.

items.says: “By 15%” repeats the change already shown by the starting and ending rates.
The line does not define what counted as a forecast hit.
items.because: Without the hit criterion, readers cannot interpret the metric.

items.says: The impact appears after the analysis detail instead of leading the bullet.
Matching repeat visitors does not establish a count of unique households.
items.because: Visitors and households are different units, and no household-level identifier or grouping method is described.

items.says: The line does not give the number of unique households it says the work counted.
The outcome appears after the data-cleaning details.
items.because: That makes it harder to spot.

items.says: The guide’s usage detail delays the point that it enabled monthly updates.
